Italian here. You have no idea how many kind of pasta and sauce actually exist.

Since everyone is talking about the usual dishes (note: 'Alfredo' is not an Italian sauce), I'll give you:

Pasta e Fagioli

You'll need:

  • Any kind of medium-small pasta you can get, let's say no larger than 1 inch.

  • Pre-cooked white beans, about 1/2 of the quantity of pasta used.

  • Bacon! About 1/3 of the quantity of beans used. No thin slices, use thick pieces that can be chopped to cubes.

  • The best olive oil you can get. Don't accept compromises, it's really important.

  • Black pepper, garlic, a small onion, oregano, sage and rosemary for seasoning; preferably fresh, otherwise use 2x the quantities. NOTE: sage must be fresh leaves, otherwise don't use it.

  • White wine or beer.

  • A wok or any large and deep pan.

  • A tall pot.

How it's done:

  • Chop the onion, the bacon, the oregano and the rosemary; of course don't use the woody parts.

  • Clean 1 clove of garlic, don't chop it.

  • Put the pan on a low flame with a little olive oil in it, let it warm up, then put inside it the onion, bacon, sage, oregano, rosemary and garlic, and wait until the bacon turns bright pink (don't make it crisp).

  • Add 1/2 glass of white wine/beer, turn the flame to max, and wait until it no longer smells like alcohol. Don't make it burn!

  • Take away the sage leaves (!important!), then add the beans' water only. Don't add the beans yet or they'll cook twice and get mushy. We'll add them later. Add 1 glass of water and 1/2 teaspoon of salt for serving, the cover the pan again.

  • Fill half the pot with water and make it boil, then add salt.

  • When the salt is melted, add the pasta. Use a spoon to fish the clove of garlic out of the pan and discard it. Then add the beans.

  • When the pasta is half-done (no longer hard but not cooked yet), add it to the pan and get the flame to max again. Don't discard the cooking water.

  • Let the pasta finish cooking together with all other ingredients. Add its cooking water and stir it if it gets too dry, just like it was a risotto. The whole thing has to be creamy, so don't add too much water either.

  • When it's done, dish it up by adding a tablespoon of olive oil and 2 or 3 pinches of grounded black pepper for each serving. Only use quality oil; if you don't have quality olive oil, just don't add any. Don't add any other seasoning on it or you'll be hit by multiple ancient Italian curses.

You're welcome.
